newsitem.title: JAPAN: DDI, NTT agree on lower access fees for PHS phones.
newsitem.headline: DDI, NTT agree on lower access fees for PHS phones.

text.p: Japanese telephone operator DDI Corp group said on Monday it reached an agreement with Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp to cut the access charges DDI pays for its Personal Handyphone System.
DDI said the deal will reduce its payments to NTT by 12 to 16 billion yen in the current business year.
The DDI group had originally planned to pay 80 billion yen in access charges to NTT for using NTT facilities and local telephone networks in the business year through March 1997.

PHS is a technology halfway between cellular phones and cordless phones, with lower costs than the former and more range than the latter. One of PHS's chief drawbacks is that it cannot be used in moving vehicles.

DDI's unit, DDI Tokyo Pocket, launched its PHS service in July 1995, but is still suffering huge losses due in part to the access charges paid to NTT and lavish sales incentives offered to its distributors.
DDI said last November that it expects its PHS business to post a current loss of 83 billion yen in 1996/97.

A spokesman at DDI Tokyo Pocket said the DDI group may revise its earnings estimates for 1996/97 after studying the impact of NTT's access charge reduction and a planned elimination of DDI's subscription fees.
DDI said last week that it would scrap the 3,000-yen initial subscription fee it charges its customers. It is also considering a cut in PHS calling rates.
